title: Arakhin 15 - Sticks and Stones...But Lashon Hara Can Really Hurt Me

summary: Rabbi Hidary explores the laws of Masekhet Arakhin, specifically focusing on the fines for rape, seduction, and defamation. He discusses the severity of Lashon Hara, explaining through various sources why malicious speech is considered more damaging than physical actions.
subjects: The ten tests of the ancestors
questions: Why does the Torah require a fine for humiliation in addition to the standard fine for rape?
Why is Lashon Hara considered more severe than physical sins?
How does the Mishna differentiate between the punishment for a rapist and someone who defames his wife?
What is the connection between Lashon Hara and the plague of Sera'at?
How can one use the tongue for positive purposes?
